label: Comprehends abstract ideas and concepts
blurb: Works with an idea that has no physical form — a rule, a category, a relationship — rather than only with concrete things.

label: Considers problems outside their own experience
blurb: Reasons about a situation they have never been in, instead of only what has happened to them.

label: Makes quick and valid generalizations
blurb: Spots the rule behind a few examples and carries it correctly into a new case.

label: Sees cause and effect
blurb: Works out what led to what, and what would follow from a change.

label: Chooses and enjoys challenging tasks
blurb: Given the option of something easy or something hard, reaches for the hard one.

label: Demonstrates great curiosity; asks how, why, what if
blurb: Wonders beyond the question asked — raises their own questions and possibilities.

label: Chooses original methods
blurb: Reaches a correct answer by an unusual route, rather than the expected one.

label: Is keenly observant
blurb: Notices detail and difference that others pass over.

label: Perfectionism
blurb: Explores caring about work while handling mistakes and knowing when to finish.

label: Strong ideas, beliefs, and opinions
blurb: Explains an opinion and considers other viewpoints without needing to argue.

label: Questions authority
blurb: Asks thoughtful questions about rules and reasons, with respect and safety.

label: Motivation for and intense focus on tasks
blurb: Explores interest, effort, and strategies for staying with a chosen task.

label: Subtle sense of humor, original jokes, and puns
blurb: Plays with ideas and words in a kind, imaginative way.

label: Sensitive to the needs of others
blurb: Notices how someone may feel and suggests thoughtful ways to help.

label: Uses an extensive vocabulary precisely and appropriately
blurb: Chooses words that clearly and accurately express an age-appropriate idea.

label: Is an avid reader of books beyond grade level
blurb: Explores understanding and enjoyment of stories without treating one activity as proof of reading habits.

label: Is motivated to write even when writing is not assigned
blurb: Creates stories, poems, journals, or other original ideas by choice; young children may tell their idea aloud.

label: Recognizes points of view, moods, and intentions
blurb: Notices what a speaker or character may think, feel, or mean using clues in a short scenario.

label: Spells words accurately that are advanced for age
blurb: Explores age-appropriate sound and word patterns; pre-readers receive picture and listening activities.

label: Asks many questions about how things work
blurb: Explores causes, mechanisms, and useful questions about familiar objects and events.

label: Grasps advanced mathematical concepts for age
blurb: Works with age-appropriate quantities and relationships without rewarding speed alone.

label: Plays chess, checkers, or other strategy games
blurb: Plans ahead and compares possible moves in simple, age-appropriate game situations.

label: Enjoys putting things in categories or hierarchies
blurb: Groups familiar things by shared features and explains how smaller groups fit inside larger ones.

label: Sometimes solves problems intuitively
blurb: Finds a workable answer even when explaining every step is difficult; the activity records the answer without penalizing that difficulty.
